findings_of_fact.finding: Yes, claimant was in employment during March 2015 to September 2015.

findings_of_law.issue: Whether the action is statute barred
findings_of_law.finding: The action is statute barred under Section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Law Cap. P.17, Laws of Akwa Ibom State, 2000, as it was filed more than 3 months after the cause of action arose.
The court lacks jurisdiction to entertain the suit because it is statute barred.
No exceptions apply; the public officer's motive is irrelevant, and continuous injury exception does not apply because the claim was for a fixed period.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court determined that the cause of action accrued in September 2015 when the last allowance was due and not paid. The suit was filed on 3rd March 2016, beyond the 3-month period prescribed by Section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Law. The court found that the exceptions raised by the claimant (acting outside scope of employment, continuous injury, contract of employment, wages exception) did not apply. The court relied on case law that the motive or propriety of the public officer's act is irrelevant, and that continuous injury requires periodicity of payment, which was absent here as the claim was for a fixed period. Therefore, the suit is statute barred and the court lacks jurisdiction.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether this action is statute barred

arguments.claimant: The matter falls within exceptions: public officer acted outside scope of employment; continuous injury; contract of employment exception; wages not susceptible to Public Officers Protection Law.
arguments.defendant: The action is statute barred having been filed more than 3 months after the cause of action arose; time begins to run from date cause of action accrued.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court found that the cause of action arose in September 2015 and the suit was filed on 3rd March 2016, five months and 15 days later. The applicable law is Section 2(a) of the Public Officers Protection Law Cap. P.17, Laws of Akwa Ibom State, 2000, which requires actions to be commenced within 3 months. The court held that the exceptions raised by the claimant did not apply: the motive of the public officer is irrelevant; continuous injury requires periodicity of payment, but here the claim was for a fixed period; and claims for wages are not exempt. Thus, the action is statute barred.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: An action against a public officer for acts done in pursuance of public duty must be commenced within 3 months of the act, neglect, or default, unless it falls within recognized exceptions such as continuance of injury, which requires periodicity of payment.
issue_analysis.result: Issue resolved in favour of the defendant.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether this Court can dismiss this suit for lack of jurisdiction on account of being statute barred

arguments.defendant: Once the court lacks jurisdiction, it must dismiss the suit.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court held that jurisdiction is fundamental and absence renders proceedings null and void. Having found the suit statute barred, the court lacks jurisdiction to entertain it and must dismiss it.
issue_analysis.holding: The court lacks jurisdiction and the suit is dismissed.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A court lacking jurisdiction cannot entertain a suit and must dismiss it.
issue_analysis.result: Issue resolved in favour of the defendant; suit dismissed.

ratio_decidendi.issue: Statute bar under Public Officers Protection Law
ratio_decidendi.principle: An action against a public officer for acts done in pursuance of public duty must be commenced within 3 months of the act, neglect, or default, unless it falls within recognized exceptions such as continuance of injury, which requires periodicity of payment.
ratio_decidendi.application: The claimant's suit was filed more than 3 months after the cause of action arose, and no exception applied.
ratio_decidendi.holding: Suit is statute barred and dismissed.

legal_principles.principle: In determining whether a case is statute barred, the court is restricted to the writ of summons and statement of claim.
legal_principles.source: Kanu v. Enugu Broadcasting Service & Ors. (2014) 46 NLLR (Pt. 148) 243; Olora v. Adegbitte (2013) 1 NWLR (Pt. 1334) 45.

legal_principles.principle: The motive or propriety of a public officer's act is irrelevant in determining whether an action is statute barred under the Public Officers Protection Act.
legal_principles.context: Claimant's argument that officer acted outside scope of employment.
legal_principles.source: Rahamaniyya United (Nig.) Ltd v. Ministry for Federal Capital Territory & Ors [2009] 43 WRN 124 CA; Chigbu v. Tonimas (Nig.) Ltd [2006] 31 WRN 179.

legal_principles.principle: For the exception of 'continuance of damage or injury' to apply, there must be periodicity of payment; where payment is for a fixed period, the cause of action accrues when the last payment was due and not paid.
legal_principles.source: Bello & Ors. v. Nigeria Customs Service Board (2015) 53 NLLR (Pt. 179) 343 NIC; LUTH & MB v. Adewole [1998] 5 NWLR (Pt. 550) 406.

statutory_interpretation.statute: Public Officers Protection Law Cap. P.17, Laws of Akwa Ibom State, 2000
statutory_interpretation.interpretation: Actions against public officers must be commenced within 3 months of the act, neglect, or default, or in case of continuance of damage or injury, within 6 months after the ceasing thereof.
statutory_interpretation.application: Claimant's suit was filed more than 3 months after the cause of action arose, and no exception applied, so it is statute barred.
